newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse ends week 4.8 percent higher.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse ends week 4.8 percent higher.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange closed the week on Friday 4.8 percent higher with the main focus on privatisation bonds, mortgage bank, and holdings and, a stockbroker said.
The all-share index closed at 598.64 from 570.96 points last Friday.

"Privatisation bonds, Credit Immobilier et Hotelier, Wafabank, ONA group and Societe Nationale d'Investissement accounted for a significant share of the trade this week," a broker at the Casablanca-based Safa bourse said.
Mortgage bank CIH closed at 324 dirhams from 282 dirhams last week.
It issued on Friday 250 million dirhams ($26.8 million) bonds in 15-year state-guaranteed debenture bonds at a rate of 10.25 percent.
Banque Nationale pour le Developpement Economique closed at 209 dirhams from 203 dirhams last week.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest conglomerate which holds diversified stakes in more than 40 firms, closed at 717 dirhams from 678 dirhams from last Friday.
ONA group, the country's largest private holding, closed at 750 dirhams from 720 dirhams, the week before.
Leading stock Wafabank traded at 810 dirhams from 750 dirhams.
Leasing firm Maroc-Leasing, which was listed on the bourse late in February, took 47 dirhams on the week to close at 359 dirhams.
Newly-floated credit firm Credor rose to 710 dirhams from 650 dirhams last week.
The over the counter market was much calmer on Friday with 6,000 shares in credit firm Eqdom and 10,500 in fertilizer company FERT.CS traded, stockbrokers said.
The volume for the unofficial market in shares and bonds and a small gold trade totalled 47.6 million dirhams from 106.8 million dirhams last Friday.
This Friday there were seven contracts involving 41 bonds for a total of 4,392,800 dirhams, and 13 contracts for 41,671 shares worth 43,247,208 dirhams.
Traded volume on the official market was 66.3 million dirhams from 69.6 million dirhams last Friday.
Friday's official market was made up of 238 deals involving 62,797 shares with a total value of 60,200,081 dirhams, 10 deals involving 1,700 privatisation bonds valued at 3,982,588 dirhams.
